text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Namibia's hopes of securing the extradition from South Africa of two suspects in connection with the bombing of U.N. offices in 1989 are fading. Leonard Veenendal and Darryl Stopforth made last-minute amnesty applications to South Africa's "truth commission" for crimes committed while Namibia was still under Pretoria's rule.
- Namibia is to use a N$93.8 million soft loan from Germany to finance waste-water reclamation in Windhoek and the extension of Walvis Bay harbour.
- The cabinet has approved Namibia's decentralisation policy, which aims to spread functions and development to the regions, within the unitary state framework.
- The Namibian govenrment is to seek foreign help in trying to probe allegations of embezzlement of drought aid.
